content.text: Gumroad's payout schedule means you wait a week or a month to access money you already earned. PayPal's conversion rates take 3 to 5 percent of every international transfer. Wire transfers cost $20 to $50 each way and take three to seven business days. These are not small frictions — they are structural extraction from creators already operating in harder markets. USDT on Tron eliminates all of this. Settlement in under 60 seconds. Fee under $0.10. The full USD equivalent of your product price lands in your wallet the moment the on-chain transaction confirms. [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/nowpayments-integration-static-site-crypto-payments-first-principles-5|NOWPayments Integration]] converts the buyer's chosen [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/crypto-payment-gateways-digital-products-every-detail-you-5|crypto]] to your configured wallet address automatically. No manual verification. No waiting. P2P conversion to local currency at near-market rates completes the pipeline — typically within 30 minutes of the original sale.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Setting Up a NOWPayments Digital Store: The Full Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-setting-up-nowpayments-digital-store-works-how-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: Setting Up a NOWPayments Digital Store: The Full Guide

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to unlocking seamless digital commerce lies in sovereign infrastructure. By leveraging tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase, you can deploy a fully operational online store with automatic crypto payment processing and instant product delivery, all while maintaining full data ownership. This approach is particularly crucial for creators in regions where conventional payment platforms are restricted or unreliable.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you begin deploying your sovereign digital commerce stack, you'll need to ensure you have a few essential components in place. This includes a GitHub account for hosting, a basic [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/understanding-kyc-payment-gateways-digital-sellers-plain-language-14|COREMERCH guide to understanding]] of Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, and a Supabase instance for order storage. You'll also need to set up a NOWPayments account to facilitate automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, with its competitive 0.5% fee structure.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

With your foundational components in place, you can start setting up your payment and delivery pipeline. This involves configuring your NOWPayments account to receive USDT payments on Tron or Solana, and integrating it with your Cloudflare Workers backend. You'll also need to set up your product delivery system, using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for secure and efficient file distribution.
Break free from platform restrictions with sovereign digital commerce infrastructure.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

The fee structure of NOWPayments is fundamentally different from conventional platform fees. NOWPayments charges 0.5% per transaction. There is no monthly fee, no setup fee, no payout fee, and no minimum transaction volume requirement. Network fees for the underlying blockchain transaction are paid by the buyer and vary by network — Tron fees are under $0.10, Solana fees are fractions of a cent, Bitcoin fees average $1 to $5 for most transactions. For a $97 product sold through the Sovereign Starter Stack, the total transaction cost is approximately $0.49 to NOWPayments plus network fees typically under $0.10 on Tron. Compare this to Gumroad's 10% fee on the same transaction — $9.70.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your digital commerce operation grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to meet increasing demand. This involves optimizing your Cloudflare Workers backend for performance, expanding your Supabase instance to handle larger order volumes, and exploring additional payment options to diversify your revenue streams. With the right scaling strategy in place, you can continue to grow your business without relying on restrictive platforms like Stripe or Gumroad.
How do I receive crypto payments for my digital products?

To receive crypto payments for your digital products, you'll need to set up a sovereign digital commerce stack using tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase. With NOWPayments, you can receive USDT payments on Tron or Solana with transaction fees as low as under $0.10 or fractions of a cent, respectively. This approach allows you to maintain full control over your sales and payment processing, without relying on restrictive platforms.
Get paid in USDT with transaction fees as low as under $0.10 on Tron or fractions of a cent on Solana.

For creators looking to build and deploy their own sovereign digital commerce stacks, the Complete Builder Kit ($197) offers a comprehensive solution. This kit includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates needed to get started, and can be purchased directly from the Coremerch shop at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. With this kit, you can instantly download everything you need to build, deploy, and scale your digital commerce operation.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack, start by setting up your GitHub Pages site and configuring your Cloudflare Workers backend. Next, integrate your NOWPayments account and set up your product delivery system using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Then, test your infrastructure to ensure everything is functioning correctly, and finally, go live and start processing transactions. Be sure to monitor your performance and scale your infrastructure as needed to meet growing demand.

Yes, NOWPayments does not require KYC, making it a convenient option for creators who value their privacy and anonymity.
